subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Learning Club 1 – Lessons 2–3: CLIL Science – How can we classify technology?
outcomes: I can explain what technology is and how it helps us.
I can classify technology by use and by age (old or new).
I can use and make an identification key with Yes/No questions.

tf.s: Technology uses science to make things that help us.
tf.why: Science helps people invent useful things.

tf.s: A steam train is new technology.
tf.why: A steam train is old technology.
VR is a modern form of technology.

tf.s: A vacuum cleaner is technology in the house that helps us clean.
tf.why: It sucks up dust from the floor.

tf.s: We can only classify technology in one way.
tf.why: We can classify it by use and by age, and more.

tf.s: A smartphone uses the internet and is new technology.
tf.why: That is two ways to classify it.

tf.s: A cassette player is new technology.
tf.why: A cassette player is old technology.

tf.s: An identification key uses Yes/No questions.
tf.why: Each answer leads you to the next question.

tf.s: A usual fridge uses the internet.
tf.why: Usually no; only a smart fridge uses the internet.

tf.s: A tree diagram helps us organise things into groups.

boxes.q: Is Virtual Reality old or new technology?
Which helps us clean the house?

boxes.why: We cook food in an oven.

boxes.q: Which uses the internet and you can carry it?
boxes.why: A smartphone is small and goes online.

boxes.q: Which can you travel in and is old technology?
boxes.why: You travel in a steam train, and it is old.

boxes.q: Does a smart fridge use the internet?
boxes.why: A smart fridge connects to the internet.
To classify is to sort into groups.

boxes.q: Which is a Yes/No question for a key?
boxes.why: The answer is yes or no.

boxes.q: What does technology use to make things that help us?

hunt.q: Uses the internet, you can carry it

mcq.q: Which ways of classifying technology are in the text?
o: uses the internet, uses machines, for cooking/cleaning, old and new
mcq.why: These are the ways in the text.

o: Yes/No questions that help you identify something
a key to open a door
mcq.why: A key uses questions to find out what something is.

mcq.q: Which pair is both old technology?
mcq.why: The telephone and cassette player are old.

mcq.q: What do we use to organise technology into groups in this lesson?
mcq.why: A tree diagram shows groups and branches.

mcq.q: Classify a smartphone in two ways.
o: It uses the internet; it is new technology.
It uses steam; it is old technology.
It is for cooking; it is old.
It is for cleaning; it uses no electricity.
mcq.why: A smartphone goes online and is new.

mcq.q: Follow the key: Does it use the internet? Yes. Can you carry it? No. Which is it?
mcq.why: A computer uses the internet, but you don’t carry it around.

mcq.q: Write two ways to classify technology. Which answer is best?
mcq.why: Use and age are ways from the lesson.

mcq.q: Which question would NOT work well in an identification key?
mcq.why: Key questions must have Yes/No answers about the object.

mcq.q: A fridge usually doesn’t use the internet, but a smart fridge does. What does this show?
o: New versions of old machines can use the internet.
mcq.why: Technology changes and new types go online.

mcq.q: Another group’s key gives two answers for the same questions. What does this mean?
o: The key doesn’t work well; it needs another question.
The objects are the same thing.
mcq.why: A good key leads to only one answer each time.
